mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises the cost of capital and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not statistically distinguishable from a flat market.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered months, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 10% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility for cyclicals and drags the broader index lower over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure, which increases discount rates and erodes real earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered months, or the average return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for three consecutive months signals a weakening residential construction sector, which negatively impacts homebuilder and material stocks and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a mixed labor market where job creation is insufficient to lower the unemployment rate, signaling weak labor quality and reducing earnings expectations, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below -2% for four consecutive months signals reduced household buffer and impending consumption cutbacks, which depresses demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS annualized change < -2% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 10% level.
